STEAM PRESS — POWER LOG

On the night of 14 June 2030, at the Maison Lévrier atelier in Le Marais, tailor Lina Haddad (27) was found dead in front of a steam press. The press was on; the press cable in her hand.

The night watchman Serge Aubert found the body on his 23.10 round. The atelier closes at 20.00; those who came and went with entry cards that evening: Clémence Roux, Baptiste Lenoir, Fatou Diallo.
INCIDENT REPORT
Open the victim’s locker
Request the press’s smart socket log
Request a search warrant for Baptiste Lenoir’s office and phone

With the branch chief’s approval:

· On Baptiste Lenoir’s phone, the workshop socket’s app was opened at 21.41; the account is shared from the workshop manager.
· In the office drawer, a utility knife; on the blade, fragments of the press cable’s grey insulation.
· A deleted e-mail draft, 20.38: ‘Lina, come and talk, I’m in my office.’
· Message to Brassard at 22.06: ‘Problem solved. The Tokyo invoices are clean.’
BAPTISTE LENOIR’S OFFICE AND PHONE — SEARCH

The autopsy showed the burns were post-mortem, the socket log that the press was switched on half an hour after death, and the courtyard camera and the watchman that the car stayed until 21.54. The search, opened on two grounds, gave the knife, the phone and the message to Brassard.
If the machine’s log doesn’t match the body’s time, look for the person who set the scene.
Le Marais — June 2030

Baptiste Lenoir, Maison Lévrier’s licensing director, was running the Tokyo licence on two invoices and passing the difference through a Maison Delorme account. When the tailor Lina Haddad put the two invoices side by side, Lenoir swiped his card as if leaving, came back by the back stairs and strangled her with the tape measure. He cut the press cable, put it in her palm and switched the socket on from his phone at 21.41.
Who killed Lina Haddad?
